question: Using logarithmic differentiation, find $\frac{dy}{dx}$ for $$y=\frac{(x+1)^x}{x^{x+1}},\qquad x>0,$$ and hence evaluate the derivative at $x=1$.
explanation:
Applying Logarithmic Differentiation
Given $$y=\frac{(x+1)^x}{x^{x+1}},\qquad x>0.$$ Since $y>0$, taking logarithm on both sides gives $$\log y=x\log(x+1)-(x+1)\log x.$$ Differentiating both sides with respect to $x$, $$\frac{1}{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=\log(x+1)+\frac{x}{x+1}-\log x-\frac{x+1}{x}.$$ Therefore, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=y\left[\log(x+1)+\frac{x}{x+1}-\log x-\frac{x+1}{x}\right].$$ Substituting the value of $y$, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{(x+1)^x}{x^{x+1}}\left[\log(x+1)-\log x+\frac{x}{x+1}-\frac{x+1}{x}\right].$$

Evaluation
At $x=1$, $$y=\frac{2^1}{1^2}=2.$$ Also, $$\log2-\log1+\frac{1}{2}-2=\log2-\frac{3}{2}.$$ Hence, $$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=1}=2\left(\log2-\frac{3}{2}\right)=2\log2-3.$$

Final Result
Thus, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{(x+1)^x}{x^{x+1}}\left[\log(x+1)-\log x+\frac{x}{x+1}-\frac{x+1}{x}\right]$$ and $$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=1}=2\log2-3.$$
